# Multi-modal - Text and Audio - Spring AI - gpt-4o-audio-preview

This example demonstrates how to interact with the same model,
[the `gpt-4o-audio-preview`](https://platform.openai.com/docs/models/gpt-4o-audio-preview),
using both text and audio inputs. Please note that not all models support every
modality, and in some cases, different models may need to be used together. For
example, the `gpt-4o-audio-preview` model does not support image inputs and
therefore cannot be used to describe photographs.

The example uses [Spring AI](https://spring.io/projects/spring-ai), a Java-based
framework for building applications powered by large language models (LLMs). It
provides tools for prompt management, LLM call chaining, memory handling,
retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)—a technique that enhances responses by
incorporating external knowledge—and integration with external data sources, all
within the Java ecosystem.

[LangChain4J](https://github.com/langchain4j/langchain4j) is an alternative
framework that also offers an abstraction layer between LLMs and the
application.

This example connects to OpenAI’s ChatGPT, hosted by OpenAI. An API
key—available from [OpenAI](https://platform.openai.com/)—is required.

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

- [OpenAI API Key](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys)

## Run the example

1. OpenAI API Key

   If you have not already done so, please create an API key from
   [OpenAI API Key](https://platform.openai.com/api-keys).

   Verify that the OpenAI APIs can be successfully invoked. The following
   command assumes that the API key is stored at `~/.chatgpt/api.key`.

   ```shell
   curl https://api.openai.com/v1/chat/completions \
     --silent \
     --header "Authorization: Bearer $(cat ~/.chatgpt/api.key)" \
     --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
     --data '{
     "messages": [
       {
         "content": [
           {
             "type": "text",
             "text": "Answer the question from the attached audio file."
           },
           {
             "type": "input_audio",
             "input_audio": {
               "data": "",
               "format": "mp3"
             }
           }
         ],
         "role": "user"
       }
     ],
     "model": "gpt-4o-audio-preview",
     "modalities": [
       "text",
       "audio"
     ],
     "audio": {
       "voice": "alloy",
       "format": "mp3"
     },
     "stream": false,
     "temperature": 0.7
   }'
   ```

   This example makes use of the Spring framework. For security purposes and to
   prevent exposing the API key in documentation, the following commands assume
   the key is saved in the `.chatgpt/openai-api.yml` file within the user’s home
   directory.
   
   ```yaml
   spring:
     ai:
       openai:
         api-key: sk-proj-XXXXX
   ```

2. Build the application

   This step assumes that a valid OpenAI API Key is available at
   `~/.chatgpt/openai-api.yml`. See Step 1 for more information about how to do
   this.

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean verify
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the application was created and the dependencies
   copied.

   ```shell
   tree --prune --sort=name -L 1 './target'
   ```

   The application fat JAR file.

   ```
   ./target
   ├── multi-modal-springai-chatgpt-api-audio-and-text-1.0.0.jar
   └── multi-modal-springai-chatgpt-api-audio-and-text-1.0.0.jar.original

   1 directory, 2 files
   ```

3. Run the program

   This step assumes that a valid OpenAI API Key is available at
   `~/.chatgpt/openai-api.yml`. See Step 1 for more information about how to do
   this.

   Select an audio prompt or use one of the sample prompts located in the
   `./assets/audio` directory.

   ```shell
   tree --sort=name './assets/audio'
   ```

   Sample audio prompts.

   ```
   ./assets/audio
   ├── Prompt-1.mp3
   └── Prompt-2.mp3

   1 directory, 2 files
   ```

   Run the example using the default audio prompt
   ([`./assets/audio/Prompt-1.mp3`](./assets/audio/Prompt-1.mp3)) by not
   specifying an audio path when running the program.

   ```shell
   # Enable native access for classpath code because Netty loads native
   # libraries, and recent JDKs warn unless unnamed-module native access is
   # explicitly allowed.
   java \
     --enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED \
     -jar './target/multi-modal-springai-chatgpt-api-audio-and-text-1.0.0.jar'
   ```
